title: Birth & Childhood
teaser: Born on a Monday morning in the Bani Hashim quarter of Makkah. His mother saw a light that illuminated the palaces of Syria.

layers.title: The Birth
layers.subtitle: Monday, 9 Rabi al-Awwal, 571 CE
layers.content:
Muhammad ﷺ, the Master of all Prophets, was born in the Bani Hashim area of Makkah on Monday morning, the ninth of Rabi al-Awwal, the same year of the Elephant incident — the twentieth or twenty-second of April, 571 CE.

Ibn Sa'd reported that Muhammad's mother said: 'When he was born, there was a light that issued out of me and lit the palaces of Syria.'

His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib carried the infant to the Ka'bah, prayed to Allah and thanked Him. He called the infant Muhammad — a name not common among the Arabs. He circumcised him on the seventh day as was the custom of the Arabs.

The first woman who suckled him after his mother was Thuwaibah, the freed slave of Abu Lahab, with her son Masruh. She had suckled Hamzah bin Abd al-Muttalib before him.
layers.hadith_ref: Ibn Sa'd 1/63 — 'When he was born, there was a light that lit the palaces of Syria'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: Halimah's Care
layers.subtitle: The desert nurse and the blessed child
layers.content:
It was the general custom of the Arabs living in towns to send their children away to Bedouin wet nurses so that they might grow up in the free and healthy surroundings of the desert, developing strong bodies and acquiring the pure speech and manners of the Bedouins.

Muhammad ﷺ was entrusted to Halimah bint Abi Dhuaib from Bani Sa'd bin Bakr. She narrated: 'It was a year of drought and famine and we had nothing to eat. Every woman who came with me got a suckling infant. When we were about to depart, I said to my husband: By Allah, I do not like to go back without any infant. I should go to that orphan and I must take him. He said: There is no harm in doing so and perhaps Allah might bless us through him.'

'When I lifted him in my arms, I found enough milk in my breast. He drank to his heart's content, and so did his foster brother. My husband then went to the she-camel to milk it and found plenty of milk in it. The next morning, my husband said: By Allah, O Halimah, you must understand that you have got a blessed child.'

The barren land sprouted luxuriant grass. The animals came back satisfied and full of milk. Every blessing that came to them came through him.
layers.hadith_ref: Ibn Hisham 1/162-164 — narration of Halimah As-Sa'diyah
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: The Opening of the Chest
layers.subtitle: Purity before prophethood
layers.content:
The Prophet ﷺ stayed with Halimah until he was about four or five years old. Then, as related by Anas in Sahih Muslim, Gabriel came down, opened his chest and took out the heart. He then extracted a blood-clot out of it and said: 'That was the part of Satan in thee.' Then he washed it with the water of Zamzam in a gold basin. After that the heart was joined together and restored to its place.

The boys and playmates went running to his nurse and said: 'Verily, Muhammad has been murdered.' They rushed towards him and found him to be all right and that only his face was pale. Anas said: 'I have seen the mark that was left on his chest.'

After this event, Halimah was worried about the boy and returned him to his mother, with whom he stayed until he was six.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 94:1 — 'Did We not expand for you your chest?'
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih Muslim 1/92 — narration of Anas ibn Malik
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: Loss & Care
layers.subtitle: The orphan whom Allah guided
layers.content:
When Muhammad ﷺ was six years old, his mother Aminah decided to visit the grave of his father Abdullah in Yathrib (Madinah). She set out to cover a journey of 500 kilometers with her orphan boy, his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, and a woman servant Umm Aiman.

She spent a month there and then made her way back to Makkah. On the route, she suffered a severe illness and died in Abwa — on the road between Makkah and Madinah.

Abd al-Muttalib brought the boy to Makkah. He had warm emotions towards the boy, his orphan grandson. He was more compassionate and loving with his grandson than with his own children. A mattress was put in the shade of the Ka'bah for Abd al-Muttalib. His children used to sit around it in deference to their father, but Muhammad ﷺ used to sit on it. His uncles would try to take him back, but Abd al-Muttalib would say: 'Leave my grandson. I swear by Allah that this boy will hold a significant position.'

When Muhammad ﷺ was eight years, two months and ten days old, his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib passed away. The charge of the Prophet now passed to his uncle Abu Talib.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 93:6-8 — 'Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you? Did He not find you lost and guide you? Did He not find you poor and enrich you?'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: What the orphan's early life teaches
layers.content:
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lost his father before birth, his mother at six, his grandfather at eight. By every worldly measure, he had less than most. And yet his grandfather said of the infant: 'This boy will hold a significant position.'

The monk Bahirah recognised him at twelve years old on a trade journey to Syria. When the caravan reached Busra, Bahirah came out and said while taking the boy's hand: 'This is the master of all humans. Allah will send him with a Message which will be a mercy to all beings.'

Abu Talib asked: 'How do you know that?' He replied: 'When you appeared from the direction of Aqabah, all the stones and trees prostrated themselves, which they never do except for a Prophet.'

Every loss in the early life of the Prophet ﷺ was preparation. Every orphaning was a clearing of attachment. What appeared as deprivation was the making of the one who would say: 'I was a Prophet when Adam was between water and clay.'
layers.quran_ref: Quran 93:3 — 'Your Lord has not abandoned you, nor is He displeased'
layers.hadith_ref: At-Tirmidhi no. 3620 — narration of Bahirah the monk
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

quiz.prompt: In which year and on which day of the week was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born?

options.text: 570 CE, Friday
571 CE, Monday
572 CE, Thursday
569 CE, Monday

quiz.citation: Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — citing Nata'ijul-Afham by Al-Fulki
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about fasting on Monday and replied: 'On it I was born, and on it the Revelation descended upon me.' The day of his birth became the day of his prophethood — Monday was chosen by Allah for both.

quiz.prompt: What did Halimah's husband say after the first night with the infant Muhammad ﷺ?

options.text: 'He is a difficult child, we should return him'
'By Allah, O Halimah, you must understand that you have got a blessed child'
'Let us keep him until he is weaned'
'Something extraordinary happened in the night'

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/162-164 — narration of Halimah As-Sa'diyah
quiz.scholar_reflection: Before prophethood, before revelation, before any outward sign of greatness — a poor Bedouin woman and her husband recognised the blessing in this orphan child. The signs of Allah's chosen were visible even in infancy.

quiz.prompt: What did Gabriel say when he opened the Prophet's chest and extracted the blood-clot?

options.text: 'This is your heart, purified for prophethood'
'That was the part of Satan in thee'
'We have purified you for the message'
'Your Lord commands you to be pure'

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim 1/92 — narration of Anas ibn Malik
quiz.scholar_reflection: The chest-opening is a literal, physical event recorded in Sahih Muslim. It is not metaphorical. The Prophet's heart was physically purified before he carried the weight of revelation. Allah prepared the vessel before filling it.

quiz.prompt: What did Abd al-Muttalib say when his children tried to remove the young Muhammad ﷺ from his mattress?

options.text: 'He is my grandson and he sits where I sit'
'Leave my grandson. I swear by Allah that this boy will hold a significant position'
'This child has been blessed since birth'
'He is more dear to me than all of you'

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/168 — account of Abd al-Muttalib
quiz.scholar_reflection: His grandfather's intuition was not explained by Islam — Abd al-Muttalib was not a Muslim. Yet he saw something in his orphan grandson that his own children did not have. Allah can place recognition of greatness even in those who do not yet know its source.

quiz.prompt: What did the monk Bahirah say when he recognised the twelve-year-old Muhammad ﷺ?

options.text: 'This boy carries the signs of a great king'
'This is the master of all humans. Allah will send him with a Message which will be a mercy to all beings'
'Protect this child from the Romans and the Jews'
'I have read of this one in our books of prophecy'

quiz.scholar_reflection: A Christian monk recognised the Prophet before he recognised himself. The signs were in creation — stones and trees prostrated. Bahirah saw what Abu Talib's tribe could not see, because he knew what to look for.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ lost his father before birth, his mother at six, and his grandfather at eight. How do you understand profound loss being part of Allah's plan for the greatest person who ever lived?
quiz.slider_label: How do you relate to loss in your own life?

options.text: Loss removes attachments that would have prevented his mission
Every deprivation was replaced with something greater from Allah
It taught him the suffering of those he would later console
Allah's plan cannot be measured by what appears as loss

quiz.citation: Quran 93:6-8 — reflections on the Prophet's early life
quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah said of the Prophet: 'Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you?' He did not say 'prevent' the orphaning. He said 'shelter' within it. The shelter was real. The orphaning was also real. Both were Allah's plan.

quiz.prompt: Halimah almost did not take the infant Muhammad ﷺ because he was an orphan and no reward seemed likely. She took him only because no other option remained. What does this tell you about how Allah brings His plan about?
quiz.slider_label: How often do you see Allah's plan in what seemed like a last resort?

options.text: Allah's greatest gifts sometimes come through reluctant vessels
When all options close except one, that one is often the right door
Human calculation fails to see what Allah has arranged
The blessing came to Halimah precisely because she had no expectations

quiz.scholar_reflection: She chose him when no one else would. And through that choice, every animal she owned became blessed, every dry land around her turned green. Allah's plan did not need her enthusiasm — only her action.

quiz.prompt: The Quran was revealed to a man who had memorised no scripture, studied under no teacher, and had no formal education. What does this tell you about the nature of divine knowledge?
quiz.slider_label: How much does your understanding of knowledge come from its source?

options.text: Divine knowledge does not require human preparation to exist
The absence of prior learning proves the revelation could not have been invented
Allah chose someone uncontaminated by existing traditions
All of these — each reason points to the same source

quiz.citation: Quran 29:48 — 'You did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write one with your right hand'
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet's lack of prior scripture learning is not a gap — it is the proof. What he brought could not have come from what he read, because he read nothing. It came from where all true knowledge comes from.

quiz.prompt: Bahirah saw the Prophet's greatness in the way stones and trees prostrated. What in your daily life might be pointing to something greater that you are not trained to read?
quiz.slider_label: How attentive are you to signs in your daily life?

options.text: The signs are there — I lack the knowledge to read them
Tafakkur — reflection — is the skill that makes signs visible
Most people miss signs because they are looking for what they expect
The Quran itself is the sign that remains when all others are missed

quiz.citation: Quran 3:190 — 'In the creation of the heavens and earth are signs for those of understanding'
quiz.scholar_reflection: Bahirah spent his life reading one book — and because of that, he recognised the living embodiment of what it described. Deep familiarity with revelation makes you able to see its signs in the world around you.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet's grandfather said: 'This boy will hold a significant position' — about an eight-year-old orphan with no visible greatness. How do you see potential in people who appear to have nothing?
quiz.slider_label: How much do you judge people by their current circumstances?

options.text: Circumstances are temporary — character is the real measure
The orphan had qualities Abd al-Muttalib could see that others missed
Allah's chosen people rarely look chosen by worldly standards
Potential is invisible until someone with wisdom notices it

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/168 — Abd al-Muttalib's words about the Prophet
quiz.scholar_reflection: The grandfather of the Prophet was not a Muslim. Yet he saw what Muslims today sometimes miss — that worldly circumstances tell you almost nothing about a person's standing with Allah.
